subject: POC access & success criteria — Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nimbus-health.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC access & success criteria — Nimbus Health

Hi Tom / team,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning — really excited about the potential to run a short POC with Nimbus Health focused on improving triage response for clinical intake messages. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your engineering and security teams unblocked: 

POC goal / success criteria (as discussed):
- Integrate Redwood hosted API into your triage pipeline for a sample of 10k messages/day.
- Achieve median inference latency <= 150ms at 1-token steady-state for the evaluation prompt set.
- Maintain output quality: >= 90% label agreement vs. your manual labels on the provided eval set.
- Track cost-per-1000 tokens under $X (we'll refine once we see traffic).

Evaluation plan / timeline:
- This week (7/15): Access provisioning + kickoff meeting to share prompts and datasets.
- 7/20–7/28: Run initial ingest + baseline eval (Vivek & Nimbus engineer pairing).
- 7/29–8/5: Iterate model/config and final evaluation.

Ownership / contacts:
- Redwood: Marissa (sales lead), Vivek (solutions eng) — cc'd.
- Nimbus: please confirm primary engineering contact and security contact so we can send SSO invites and IP allowlist details.

Access provisioning we need from you (to speed setup):
1) Preferred SSO domain (Okta/Azure AD) and email addresses to invite (we can send SCIM/SSO invites).
2) If you prefer API key access instead, confirm an admin email to receive the temporary POC key.
3) Any IP ranges we should expect to allow or if you'll be doing outbound restrictions from your side.

Attachments: I attached a draft POC MOP (nimbus_poc_mop_v1.xlsx) and a short SOC2 summary for your compliance team.

Can you confirm the engineering contact and whether we should provision via SSO or temp API key? If fine, Vivek can provision the account later today.

Thanks!

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Phone: (415) 555-0183

Subject: Re: POC access & success criteria — Nimbus Health

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Appreciate the level-setting.

Quick answers:
- We’re happy to proceed. Primary engineering lead is Sarah Patel (cc’d). Security/compliance contact is IT Ops (it-ops@nimbus-health.com).
- For speed, we prefer a temporary API key for initial integration (our infra team prefers fewer SSO invites for POCs). We’ll lock things down if we extend.
- Tentative timeline looks good; target kickoff on 7/20 for pairing.

I attached our procurement questionnaire and a short note from IT on outbound proxy considerations.

Can your team provide the temp API key and a list of Redwood IPs to allow? Also please confirm the API hostname and any rate limits we should plan for during the POC.

—
Tom Ellis
Head of Product | Nimbus Health
T: 617-555-4422

Subject: Re: POC access & success criteria — Nimbus Health

Thanks Tom — great. We can do temporary API-key-based access for the initial hookup. Outline below for provisioning and next steps: 

Provisioning steps (Redwood -> Nimbus):
1) Redwood will create a temporary POC account tied to your org and issue a time-limited API key (7-day TTL by default). We’ll send the key via a secure attachment in a follow-up email.
2) If you decide to use SSO instead, we can send an Okta/Azure invite and support SCIM on request.
3) IP allowlist (suggested for inbound exceptions from Nimbus): Redwood POC egress IPs — 35.192.0.0/14, 34.96.0.0/13, and 34.120.0.0/14 (please confirm with your infra). If your team restricts outbound, let us know and we’ll provide alternate routing guidance.
4) API hostname: https://api.redwoodinference.com (region: us-west). Default POC rate-limit: 20 requests/sec, we can raise for the pairing session.

Kickoff meeting: Vivek and I can do a 60-min pairing session on Mon 7/20. Proposed times: 9am PT or 1pm PT. What works best for Sarah?

I’ve attached a short PDF with the step-by-step access guide (redwood_poc_access_steps.pdf). Vivek, can you provision the account and send the temp key to Sarah (secure attachment)?

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Tom — Vivek here from Redwood SRE/solutions. Per Marissa’s request I’ve provisioned your POC workspace and completed the initial setup. Details below: 

- Account: nimbus-poc.redwoodinference.com (internal id: NIM-POC-20260717)
- Temp API key (attached): temp_api_key.txt — KEY: redwood_poc_key_xyz123 (this key is a temporary secret and will expire in 7 days). Please rotate to a longer-lived key if you extend beyond the POC.
- IPs we used for the outbound egress allowlist: 35.192.0.0/14, 34.96.0.0/13, 34.120.0.0/14. If your stack needs specific /32s for firewall rules, let me know and I’ll provide a minimal set.
- Okta invite: sent to s.patel@nimbus-health.com (if you want SSO instead of temp key, accept the invite and I’ll complete SCIM mapping).
- Rate limits: currently set to 50 req/sec for the pairing session window (7/20 09:00–12:00 PT).

I attached the temp_api_key.txt file (expires 2026-07-24). For security we recommend pasting the key into an environment variable and not checking it into source control.

Confirm when you’ve picked a time for kickoff and that the key/API connectivity works from your side. Happy to pair during the session to instrument metrics and run the first eval script.

—
Vivek Kulkarni

- Okta invite for s.patel@nimbus-health.com arrived and SSO setup looks good — we’ll keep the temp key for local testing.
- Our security team requires us to add Redwood egress ranges to our allowlist. We’ll allow the /14 ranges you listed for the POC window and then tighten to specific /32s if needed.
- Outbound proxy on our side requires explicit hostname allow for api.redwoodinference.com — I’ve asked infra to add that.

Kickoff: 7/20 9am PT works for pairing — can we confirm a calendar invite? If possible, we’d like the session to include a short walkthrough of how you collect latency metrics and how we can push our eval set.

Thanks — Sarah
